Default enforcement behavior: Do not attribute hides, declines, or non-response to a candidate/member telemetry record. Aggregate only at a thresholded, delayed feature-surface level, with no candidate/member dimension.

Do not run behavioral A/B tests or personalized experiments on consent, block/report, withdrawal, identity, access controls, discovery, media, meeting, or safety surfaces without a separately approved governance review. Feature assignment must not reach counterpart, matching, or behavioral-profile payloads.
Keep interaction/access/comfort controls private by default and deny discovery, ranking, allocation, advertising, and profiling services access to them.
Retain topic opt-in only for the active context lifetime; do not create cross-context topic history, opt-in roster, threshold progress, or identity-linked participation profile.
Do not embed, semantically index, vectorize, or use private/member text for matching, ranking, profiling, or model training. Search may index a reviewed public prompt catalog only.
Store only a current authorization projection plus a restricted, content-minimized, purpose-limited accountability receipt. Historical consent decisions never become a behavioral profile.
Do not emit member region-change events to unrelated consumers. Do not retain ordered old/new region history. Batch/delay does not legitimize an otherwise unnecessary data flow.
No attendance, RSVP-completed, arrival, departure, no-show, plan-success, or encounter-outcome state. Expiry/cancellation ends the plan without producing an outcome record.
Use recipient-scoped, expiring disclosure. Do not transfer counterpart profiles, exact venue/address, routes, or attendance. Never feed trusted-contact actions into discovery or scoring.
One consent request, one capability, one purpose, one recipient/session scope, one expiry. Reject bundle requests in schema, API, server authorization, and UI.
Do not show participation rosters, progress bars, “waiting on” states, threshold countdowns, response timing, or participant-level topic state.
A hidden topic stays hidden until the member explicitly reverses it or the relevant context is deleted. It is not a permanent cross-platform preference profile.
Keep reviewed catalog prompts separate from member-proposed topics. Never rewrite a topic based on another member’s private text, profile, identity, behavior, or access controls.
Moderator access is case-bounded, time-bounded, role-bounded, purpose-bounded, and auditable. No general member dossier or unrestricted history view exists.
Blocking/restricting acts immediately and independently. Reporting must not alter counterpart-visible state, timing, access patterns, or notifications.

Authorization requires contract ID, named purpose, exact allowed fields, consumer identity, current policy version, retention class, revocation behavior, and audit evidence. “Policy-authorized service” alone is insufficient.
Do not permit generic none for member-sensitive data. Use explicit system-only categories such as static_public_content or policy_metadata, and reject them for member data.

Treat sensitive endpoint timing as S2a by default. Apply response-shape minimization, batching, padding where practical, and no counterpart-visible state transitions; document any remaining residual risk.
